### Hala Lacquerware (`lumenary:hala-lacquerware`, models this process)

_From: Hala, Sindh; when: Traditional craft, still practised; works best on: Pictures with rich colour._

Lacquerware is made on a lathe. While the wooden piece spins, a stick of lac, a resin that softens with heat, is held against it, and the friction melts a thin layer onto the wood. One colour after another is laid on, and fine lines are scratched through the top coat to show the colour beneath. That is why the colour runs around the piece in rings.

**How it is made, as the model does it:**

1. Draw a lathe-turned piece in the dark: a vase, a cylinder or an egg-shaped jar, with a soft shadow at its foot.
2. Map each pixel at horizontal offset dx from the axis to an angle φ = arcsin(dx/ρ) on the surface of the cylinder, where ρ is the piece’s half-width at that height.
3. Wrap the picture round the piece by reading it at x = W (½ + φ/π), so it takes half a turn to run across your picture and it is squeezed near the edge.
4. Fill every band (as tall as the band slider times 1.3 px) with a single colour averaged from the picture.
5. Scratch fine lines through the top coat, and add the sheen of polished lac.

**The maths:**

$$u=\frac{x-x_c}{\rho(y)},\qquad \varphi=\arcsin u,\qquad x_{\text{src}}=W\Big(\tfrac12+\frac{\varphi}{\pi}\Big)$$

_Wrapping the picture round a cylinder. u runs from −1 to 1 across the piece and x_src is where the picture is read. Without “wrap” it is read at x._ (primitives: coordinate-warp)

$$\frac{dx}{d\varphi}=\rho\cos\varphi\ \ \Rightarrow\ \ \text{picture density}\propto\frac{1}{\cos\varphi}$$

_Why the picture looks squeezed near the sides: equal steps of angle cover less and less width on screen._ (primitives: coordinate-warp)

$$\rho_{\text{egg}}(t)=0.45\,W\,\sin^{0.55}\!\big(\pi(0.04+0.92\,\hat t)\big),\qquad \rho_{\text{cyl}}=0.33\,W$$

_Two of the three profiles; t̂ runs 0 to 1 over the height of the piece. The vase profile is a sum of smoothstep curves._ (written for this model: specific)

$$f=(0.3+0.7\cos\varphi)\,\big(1-0.45\operatorname{smoothstep}(0.82,1,|u|)\big),\qquad s=0.75\,e^{-\left(\frac{u+0.42}{0.16}\right)^2}+0.3\,e^{-\left(\frac{u-0.68}{0.07}\right)^2}$$

_Shading and the two highlights, a broad one on the left and a narrow one on the right. The highlight is added with weight equal to the polish slider._ (primitives: cylinder-shading, soft-threshold)

**Dials:** `shape` (Piece) = "vase" (vase, cylinder, egg); `band` (Band width) = 6 [2 to 14]; `detail` (Colour follows picture) = 55 [0 to 100]; `scratch` (Scratched lines) = 70 [0 to 100]; `polish` (Polish) = 65 [0 to 100]; `wrap` (Wrap the picture round) = true.

**History:** Lac is the resin made by tiny insects and used for centuries across South Asia for lacquer and sealing wax. In Sindh the craft of lacquered, lathe-turned wood is closely tied to Hala, where bed legs, cradles, toys and boxes are made. It is a craft of family workshops, and demand for it has been under pressure from cheaper goods.
